title: Diagnose Distributed AI Workload Failures with NVIDIA Attribution | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA open-sourced NVIDIA Attribution, a deterministic, workload-centric system that correlates logs, metrics and scheduler state to pinpoint the root cause of distributed AI job failures (e.g., an NVLink XID 149 fault behind cascading NCCL errors). It has run in production for years, analyzing millions of workloads weekly across hundreds of thousands of GPUs, and is split into a REST Service and a connector-based Blueprint.

insights.claim: In distributed AI workloads, one GPU or fabric fault cascades into NCCL errors on other ranks, scheduler state changes and thousands of downstream messages, so the reported exception shows where the job stopped rather than where the failure began.
insights.speaker: Gargi Prasad
insights.so_what: Misattributed failures waste repair effort and GPU time; accurate diagnosis is a lever on AI cluster utilization.
insights.quote: The reported exception shows where the workload stopped, not where the failure began.
insights.locator: In distributed AI workloads, a single error

insights.claim: NVIDIA Attribution analyzes failures in the context of a workload rather than as isolated node events, returning outcome, root cause, affected nodes, supporting symptoms and an evidence trail.
insights.speaker: Gargi Prasad
insights.so_what: Workload-centric diagnosis connects hardware faults to lost training progress, the unit investors' customers actually pay for.
insights.quote: Workload-centric means analyzing failures in the context of a workload rather than as isolated node events.

insights.claim: In a worked example, an XID 149 NVLink signal integrity fault on one node is identified as the root cause while three NCCL errors across ranks are demoted to supporting symptoms, and the job is classified as a hardware failure rather than independent communication errors.
insights.speaker: Gargi Prasad
insights.so_what: Shows NVLink interconnect signal integrity as a real failure mode in NVIDIA's rack-scale systems.
insights.quote: The workload is reported as a hardware failure rather than a set of independent communication errors.

insights.claim: The rule set includes a GB200-specific root-cause prioritization rule (Gb200PriorityRootCause), indicating the attribution logic is tuned to NVIDIA's GB200-generation systems.
insights.speaker: Gargi Prasad
insights.so_what: Platform-specific failure handling suggests new rack-scale generations bring new failure signatures needing dedicated tooling.
insights.locator: Refine the symptoms into one attribution

insights.claim: NVIDIA Attribution has been used in production across NVIDIA AI infrastructure for years and analyzes millions of workloads each week across hundreds of thousands of GPUs.
insights.speaker: Gargi Prasad
insights.so_what: Signals the scale of NVIDIA's internally operated GPU infrastructure and the maturity of the tool being open-sourced.
insights.quote: analyzes millions of workloads each week across hundreds of thousands of GPUs
insights.locator: Used in production across NVIDIA AI infrastructure

insights.claim: In one large RDMA-backed cluster, NVIDIA Attribution correlated port errors, connection resets and scheduler events to find patterns around specific host and switch ports, guiding targeted fabric repairs and congestion tuning.
insights.speaker: Gargi Prasad
insights.so_what: Networking fabric is a material reliability bottleneck in AI clusters, supporting demand for network diagnostics and repair.
insights.quote: helping teams target fabric repairs and congestion tuning
insights.locator: Used in production across NVIDIA AI infrastructure

insights.claim: NVIDIA Attribution uses deterministic rules rather than opaque inference, making diagnoses reproducible and customizable, with structured output for integration into health and recovery systems.
insights.speaker: Gargi Prasad
insights.so_what: Deterministic, auditable diagnosis is favored for operating expensive infrastructure, a contrast to purely AI-driven ops tooling.
insights.quote: Deterministic rules make the results reproducible and customizable

insights.claim: When multiple causes fit the evidence the attributed domain is marked ambiguous, because attribution quality depends on telemetry quality and completeness.
insights.speaker: Gargi Prasad
insights.so_what: Telemetry completeness becomes a prerequisite for automated ops, implying demand for observability infrastructure.
insights.quote: Quality of attribution is dependent on the quality and completeness of the underlying telemetry.
insights.locator: When multiple causes fit the evidence

insights.claim: Rule changes are committed and shipped with the Service and are not uploaded dynamically via the HTTP API, with inline test cases evaluated at startup.
insights.speaker: Gargi Prasad
insights.so_what: Governance-first design suits regulated or sovereign operators who need controlled change management.
insights.quote: rules are not uploaded dynamically through the HTTP API
insights.locator: At startup, the Service loads the bundled rule catalog

insights.claim: NVIDIA Attribution is split into a self-hosted Attribution Service exposing the engine via HTTP/REST API and a Python Attribution Blueprint reference orchestrator that handles cluster-specific scheduler, telemetry and output connectors.
insights.speaker: Gargi Prasad
insights.so_what: Separating core logic from integrations lets NVIDIA standardize diagnosis across heterogeneous customer clusters.
insights.quote: This separation lets teams apply the same attribution logic across clusters while adapting scheduler, telemetry, and output connectors to each environment.
insights.locator: The attribution engine contains the rules engine

insights.claim: The Blueprint ships with connectors for Slurm, Kueue, Loki, Kubernetes pod logs, PromQL metrics, local files, stdout and SQLite.
insights.speaker: Gargi Prasad
insights.so_what: Broad connector coverage across Slurm and Kubernetes ecosystems lowers adoption barriers for NVIDIA's ops software.

insights.claim: Open-sourcing NVIDIA Attribution lets infrastructure teams encode a failure pattern once and apply it across workloads and clusters, routing results into incident, recovery and fleet-management systems.
insights.speaker: Gargi Prasad
insights.so_what: Community-contributed failure rules could make NVIDIA's diagnosis layer a de facto standard in AI factory operations.
insights.quote: Open sourcing NVIDIA Attribution enables infrastructure teams to encode a failure pattern once and apply it across workloads and clusters.

insights.claim: NVIDIA Attribution complements readiness checks, continuous health monitoring and infrastructure-repair and workload-restart systems within NVIDIA's health and resilience software.
insights.speaker: Gargi Prasad
insights.so_what: Shows NVIDIA building a full-stack resilience software suite around its hardware.
insights.quote: It complements readiness checks, continuous health monitoring, and the systems that repair infrastructure and restart workloads.
insights.locator: NVIDIA health and resilience software helps teams
